# Song and deployed models comparison implementation plan

**Goal:** Run a reproducible, paired comparison of the project's demand/pricing methods and its Song reimplementation, with charts and raw artifacts. Do not edit Word.

**Architecture:** Add a separate package at `experiments/comparison_v3`; reuse verified V2 panels, `SongTransformer`, the serving ARIMAX equation/feedback and the train-fitted kernel simulators. Keep all new outputs under `experiments/artifacts/comparison_v3`. Never overwrite Phase 5/6 or serving artifacts.

**Tech stack:** Python, NumPy, pandas, statsmodels, PyTorch, Stable-Baselines3, matplotlib, unittest.

**Spec:** The user's approved comparison procedure in this chat: same data/keys/bounds, train-only preprocessing, validation selection, matched PPO interaction budgets, paired seeds, two independent train-fitted simulators, uncertainty intervals and charts. Existing V2 test has been inspected; label new results exploratory, not an untouched confirmatory holdout.

## Rulings and constraints

- Work additively in the requested current repository on branch `Thong`, without a worktree: ignored data and user edits are needed here; no existing application file will be changed.
- Five seeds: 42, 123, 456, 789, 1024. Report limited independent replication, never count weekly decisions as independent training runs.
- User explicitly selected full M5, not a 60-series sample. Forecast all 29,069 eligible series and all 1,220,898 frozen test keys. Pricing covers all train-fit ARIMAX/kernel-eligible series with causal initial history; report ineligible series and reasons rather than calling these all 29,069 price-sensitive products.
- Train-only scalers, fit scope and frozen evaluation keys are shared by all methods in each comparison. Do not silently drop ARIMAX fit failures: report coverage and fallback for forecasts; pricing failures must stop or be explicitly excluded before looking at held-out outcomes.
- Demand pretraining uses the fixed Song 4-layer, 8-head, 128-width architecture; validation early stopping with a materially larger maximum epoch budget than Phase 5. Save train/validation learning curves and convergence/budget warnings.
- Pricing compares fixed train mean, fixed upper train price, ARIMAX grid, ARIMAX PPO and Song feedback PPO. Same train simulator, interaction budget, initial history, train price range, evaluation calendar and common random draws. Each policy owns its evolving simulated history and model feedback.
- Persist checkpoints and exact run configuration with hashes. Reuse only when configuration/data/code identity matches. Save individual predictions, decisions and run totals, plus CSV/PNG charts and a factual README.

## Tasks

- [x] 1. Tests and data/statistics contract. Check train-only cohort selection; key mismatch rejection; paired seed matching; bootstrap reproducibility; causality of pricing history; feedback isolation.
- [x] 2. Implement data loader, forecast training/metrics, serving adapters and matched pricing training/evaluation. Save resumable units and provenance. Test real small fixture training and serialize/reload parity.
- [x] 3. Execute dependency/hardware preflight, verified panel preparation, actual comparative runs and chart generation. Inspect plots, rerun targeted tests and report actual findings and limitations.

## Verification and review focus

- Expected failure before implementation, then green contract tests.
- Same keys for every model/seed, no duplicate decisions; finite outputs and valid action bounds.
- Test-label corruption does not change cohort, scalers, trained models, price actions or validation selections.
- Paired uncertainty resamples complete seed runs (and optionally fixed-cohort SKU units), not individual correlated weeks.
- Common noise is independent of policy RNG; no leakage of actual test quantities into simulated rollouts.
- Training resumes only from saved complete units with matching identities; incomplete units are never displayed as complete comparisons.
- Mark every chart as exploratory V2 rerun and label cohort, units, uncertainty scope and missing methods.
